# @vantreeseba/graphql-mocks

> An npm-workspaces monorepo for the `@vantreeseba/graphql-mocks` toolkit: generate realistic, graph-connected mock data from a GraphQL schema using faker, answer any operation from that graph, and type the pools with a companion GraphQL Code Generator plugin.

The runtime introspects every object type in a `GraphQLSchema` (or SDL string) and produces a set of interconnected mock objects where relationships are honored as real object references — `User.todos` references actual mocked `Todo` objects, and `Todo.user` points back to a `User`. Because the result is a graph rather than unrelated fixtures, an arbitrary query can be answered from it: the selection set decides what comes back. Useful for tests, demos, and Storybook mocking. The codegen plugin emits a `SchemaTypeMap` (`{ TypeName: GeneratedType }`) you pass as `TTypes` to `buildMocks` so pools come back typed without a cast.

Key facts:
- TypeScript 5, strict mode, ESM only.
- Two published packages, versioned and released together via semantic-release: `@vantreeseba/graphql-mocks` (runtime) and `@vantreeseba/graphql-mocks-codegen` (codegen plugin).
- Runtime peer deps: `graphql >=16`, `@faker-js/faker >=9` (plus optional `@graphql-typed-document-node/core >=3` for the Apollo helpers and `@apollo/client >=3.8 <5` for the `./apollo` subpath — the root entry never imports it). Codegen peer deps: `graphql >=16`, `@graphql-codegen/plugin-helpers >=5`, `@graphql-codegen/visitor-plugin-common >=5`.
- Not a server: mutations resolve but never write to the pool, and nothing persists between calls.

## Documentation

- [How to use this library](https://github.com/cubicecho/graphql-mocks/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md): The guided path — install, first pool, answering an operation, rendering a component against it, typed pools, shaping the data, the states worth covering, and the behaviours that surprise people (cyclic pools, opt-in arguments, the `result.data` trap, empty staying empty).
- [Monorepo overview](https://github.com/cubicecho/graphql-mocks/blob/main/README.md): Packages table and documentation index.
- [Runtime reference: @vantreeseba/graphql-mocks](https://github.com/cubicecho/graphql-mocks/blob/main/packages/graphql-mocks/README.md): `buildMocks` API and every option (count, seed, nullChance, scalars, overrides, derive, deriveObject, relations, countFields, scenario, resolveType, addTypename, stableIds, idPrefix, listSize, uniqueLists, qa, matchArguments, argOverrides), argument matching, wrapper/connection types, the request handler and Apollo integration, mock validation, QA mode, scenarios and the matrix, typed pools, and helpers.
- [Codegen plugin: @vantreeseba/graphql-mocks-codegen](https://github.com/cubicecho/graphql-mocks/blob/main/packages/graphql-mocks-codegen/README.md): generating a `SchemaTypeMap`, plugin configuration (`typeMapName`, `typesImportPath`, `typesNamespace`), and generated output.
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/cubicecho/graphql-mocks/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md): Setup, commands, repo layout, conventions, commit format, git workflow, and how releases are cut.
- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/cubicecho/graphql-mocks/blob/main/AGENTS.md): Project structure, stack and conventions, for coding agents.

## API

- `buildMocks(schema, options?)`: Core entry point. Accepts a `GraphQLSchema` or SDL string; returns a `MockResult` keyed by object-type name. Generic `buildMocks<TTypes>(schema)` returns typed pools.
- `MockResult.find(typeName, predicate)`: Find a single mocked item; the item is typed when a `TTypes`/`SchemaTypeMap` is supplied, or `find<T>('Type', …)` for a typed one-off.
- `MockResult.toResolvers()`: Produce Apollo Server / GraphQL Yoga mock resolvers (`{ Type: () => <random item from pool> }`) for `addMocksToSchema`.
- `MockResult.dataForOperation(document, variables?, matchArguments?)`: Execute a query/mutation against the graph and return data shaped to the selection set (lists, fragments, and interface/union fields supported). Return type inferred from a `TypedDocumentNode`. Results are acyclic — only pooled objects are cyclic. Not idempotent: each call re-resolves and draws from the shared seeded faker, so repeated calls differ in rows and in list length — use `dataOf` to read what a built mock carries.
- `MockResult.resolveOnce(document, variables?, matchArguments?)`: `dataForOperation` memoized on the graph — the first call resolves, later calls with the same document object and the same variables return that same result. For reading *the* rows a document stands for, without a hand-rolled `Map<DocumentNode, unknown>`. Keyed by document identity (a re-`parse` is a different document) plus the variables and `matchArguments` given with it.
- `MockResult.toRequestHandler(options?)` / `createRequestHandler(mocks, options?)`: A handler answering any operation from the graph with no registration — memoized per document+variables, with ordered `overrides` (`data`/`errors`/`networkError`/`loading`/`delay`/`once`), a `calls` spy list and `reset()`.
- `mockLink(mocksOrHandler, options?)` from `@vantreeseba/graphql-mocks/apollo`: wrap a graph or handler in an `ApolloLink`.
- `createMockClient(source, options?)` from `./apollo`: a whole `ApolloClient` — `mockLink` plus a fresh `InMemoryCache` per call and `fetchPolicy: 'no-cache'` / `errorPolicy: 'all'` for `query` and `watchQuery`. `defaultOptions` is a deep partial (`PartialDefaultOptions`) merged per operation kind then per key, so `{ mutate: { errorPolicy: 'all' } }` alone is a whole valid value. Accepts a `MockResult`, a `MockRequestHandler`, or a `(options) => MockResult` factory; factory-built graphs are memoized per config.
- `withGraphqlMocks(source, { wrap, parameterName?, clientKey? })` / `resolveMockClient(source, parameter, base?)` from `./apollo`: a Storybook decorator resolving the `graphqlMocks` story parameter (`true | 'loading' | 'errored' | { state, target, build, qa, …handler options } | false`) into a memoized client. The memo is keyed by story (`context.id`) and parameter, so a re-render reuses one client while every story keeps its own `InMemoryCache`; `clientKey: (context) => string` replaces the story identity to share one client across a set of stories. Renderer-free — `wrap: (client, Story, context) => …` is supplied by the caller.
- `toMockClientParameter(parameter)` / `withState(parameter, state)` / `withQa(parameter, qa)` from `./apollo`: derive one story parameter from another without branching on which form it is. `toMockClientParameter` is the long form of any accepted parameter, read exactly as the decorator reads it (absent and `true` are `{ state: 'default' }`); `withState` / `withQa` are parameter-in / parameter-out and keep the base's `overrides`, `target`, `build` and handler options, and return `false` for a story that opted out.
- `mockScenarios(base?, target?)`: the `default` / `loading` / `errored` trio of `MockHandlerOptions`, optionally narrowed to specific operations.
- `MockResult.mockOperationsFrom(module, options?)`: map a codegen document module's export names to lazily built variants.
- `MockResult.ids(type)` / `.at(type, index)` / `.byId(type, id)`: address pooled items directly.
- `MockResult.byIdOrIndex(type, key)`: the "either" lookup for a key that might be an id, might be a numeric index, and might be missing — the item with that id, else the item at that index when the key reads as a whole one in range, else element 0. Returns the element **non-optionally**, so it replaces the `byId(…) ?? at(…) ?? at(…, 0)` chain and the cast that chain forces. Throws a `RangeError` on an empty pool, where there is no element 0 to fall back to.
- `paginate(items, args)` / `searchItems(items, term, fields?)`: the array primitives the argument engine uses, exported for wrapper types it cannot reach. A `searchItems` field is a key, a dotted path through relations (`'author.name'`, stepping through lists), or an accessor; a missing link is a non-match. Omitting `fields` searches own string properties only and never follows relations.
- `toPlain(value, options?)` / `select(value, document, options?)`: cycle-safe views of pooled objects — a deep copy that cuts references back into the path being copied (`onCycle: 'stub' | 'null' | 'omit'`, `maxDepth`), and a projection onto a document's selection set that is cycle-free by construction. `toPlain` returns the type it was given; `select` infers its result from a `TypedDocumentNode`.
- `validateMocks(mocks, options?)` / `assertValidMocks(...)`: check hand-written Apollo mocks for the shapes that fail silently — a resolver parked at `result.data`, an unparsed query, a missing `result`/`error`, functions inside `data`. Takes one mock, an array, a variants trio, or a whole module namespace; both walks are cycle-safe, so a module may export a built pool alongside its mocks. `requireData: false` allows empty payloads, `probeVariables` calls a resolver-form `result` and validates what it returns. Each issue carries `kind`: `'invalid'` for a mock that was checked and is wrong, or the single `'empty'` report meaning no mocks were found at all. A `mockOperationsFrom` map is walked like any other module, forcing its lazy entries, so check it in a test rather than in the module.
- `mockOperation(query, data, options?)` / `mockOperationVariants(...)`: Build Apollo `MockedProvider` `MockedResponse` entries from supplied result data (`options`: `variables`, `delay`, `error`, `maxUsageCount`); the trio is `withResults` / `withLongLoadTime` / `withError`. `data` may instead be a `(variables) => data` resolver, producing a `DynamicMockedResponse`.
- `dataOf(mock, variables?)`: Unwrap an Apollo mock envelope to its `TData`, non-optionally — replaces the `mock.result?.data?.x ?? []` chain whose fallback hides a renamed field. Throws for the `withError` variant or an envelope with no `result`/`data`; `withLongLoadTime` carries the same data as `withResults` and returns. For a resolver-form mock the variables are passed to the resolver (default `{}`).
- `MockResult.mockOperation(query, options?)` / `MockResult.mockOperationVariants(...)`: Same, but resolve the result data from the `MockResult` graph (via `dataForOperation`) so the query's selection set selects the mocks — no data argument needed. Adds `dynamic`, `transform` and a per-call `matchArguments`.
- Option types (each taking the same optional `TTypes` map as `buildMocks`, which binds its keys to the schema): `CountConfig`, `OverridesConfig` / `OverrideContext` / `FieldOverrideFn`, `DeriveConfig` / `DeriveContext` / `FieldDeriveFn`, `ObjectDeriveConfig` / `ObjectDeriveContext` / `ObjectDeriveFn`, `RelationsConfig` / `RelationContext` / `RelationFn` / `RelationSpec` / `RelationSize`, `CountFieldsConfig`, `QaConfig` / `QaOption` / `QaProfileName`, `ArgOverride` / `ArgOverrideMatch` / `ArgOverrideData` / `ArgOverrideContext`, `ArgMatchingOptions`, `ListSizeConfig`, `UniqueListsConfig`, `StableIdsConfig`, `ScalarMocker`, `Scenario` / `ScenarioMap`, `MockResult`, `MockHelpers`. A config can therefore be declared away from the `buildMocks` call and still be checked. In `overrides` and `derive` the map is a hint rather than a closed contract: type names are checked against it, a field it does not carry is accepted with an `unknown` return (and, for a derive, a still-typed `self`), and a misspelled field name therefore reads as an unmapped one. `MockResult` is unchanged — pooled instances are typed by the map alone.
- `BuildMocksOptions`: `count`, `faker`, `seed`, `nullChance`, `scalars`, `overrides`, `fieldOverrides`, `aliases`, `derive`, `deriveObject`, `relations`, `countFields`, `scenario`, `resolveType`, `addTypename`, `stableIds`, `idPrefix`, `qa`, `listSize`, `uniqueLists`, `matchArguments`, `argOverrides`.
- `fieldOverrides` option (`Record<fieldName, (faker, ctx) => value>`): overrides keyed by field name instead of by type, applied to every mocked type carrying that field — one entry covers `imageUrl` wherever it appears. A key wrapped in slashes is a regular expression (`'/Url$/'`, `'/^is[A-Z]/i'`). Precedence is a type-keyed `overrides` entry, then an exact name, then patterns in declaration order. Fires on relationship fields too, and a key matching no field on any mocked type warns (root fields are not covered — use `relations`/`argOverrides`).
- `aliases` option (`{ [type]: { [field]: string | string[] } }`): also exposes a field under the name a fragment aliases it to (`{ User: { addresses: 'locations' } }`), since a pooled `User` has `addresses` while the generated fragment type has `locations` — a component reads `undefined` and renders empty with no type error. The alias holds the same reference, not a clone, and is applied last, after relationships, counts and derives. An unknown type or field, an operation or non-object type, or an alias colliding with a real field throws.
- `overrides` vs `derive`: an `overrides` function runs while the instance is half-built (arguments `(faker, { index, typeName, fieldName })`), so it cannot see its siblings. A `derive` function runs last — after scalars, overrides, relationship wiring and reciprocal mirroring — with the finished object as `self` (`(self, { index, typeName, fieldName, faker })`), so it wins over an `overrides` entry for the same field and is where totals, assembled names and differences belong.
- `deriveObject` option (`{ [type]: (self, { index, typeName, faker }) => object }`): one function per type, run once per instance, returning a partial merged over the generated object — for fields that come from a **single** correlated draw (`subtotal`/`tax`/`total`), which a per-field `derive` cannot express because each field takes the shared faker stream as it comes. Runs in the same phase as `derive` and sees the same finished object; within a type it runs first, so a `derive` for a key it returned wins and reads the correlated values off `self`. Both beat `overrides`. An omitted key stays as generated, a nullish return leaves the instance untouched, and scenario layers merge it one level deep (per type, later function wins).
- `relations` option (`RelationsConfig`): shapes relationship fields after every pool exists — a number, a `{ min, max }` range, `null` (empty), `'all'` (the whole target pool), a `{ size, where }` filter, or `(ctx) => value` picking the related objects from `ctx.pool`. A `{ size, where }` spec draws only from the pooled objects `where(item, ctx)` keeps and sizes the draw with `size` (any ordinary spec; the usual sizing when absent) — a predicate that matches nothing throws, a singular field cycles by the owner's index, and on a root field `where` narrows the pool that argument matching, paging and the random pick then work against. The predicate is `RelationPredicate<T>` (`(item, ctx) => unknown`), typed from the related field when a `TTypes` map is in play and defaulting to the loose pooled record otherwise, so a `where` needs no cast. Resolved `[type][field]` → `[type]._default` → `_default` → the flat form, and it reaches root fields through the operation type (`{ Query: { users: 3 } }`). Beats `nullChance` and the QA `lists` profile; `overrides` still beats it. Pools grow to meet demand. Config errors throw (`TypeError` for an unknown/ineligible field or an emptied non-null singular field, `RangeError` for a bad size). `{ _reciprocal: true }` opts into writing each reference back into its inverse field; `'hidden'` wires those back-references as non-enumerable properties.
- `listSize` option (`ListSizeConfig`): how many items every generated list field holds — scalar, enum, relationship and root alike. A flat `3` or `{ min, max }` sizes every list in the graph; a map takes the same shape as `relations` (`{ Post: { tags: 2, _default: 4 }, Query: { posts: 3 }, _default: { min: 1, max: 5 } }`) and resolves `[type][field]` → `[type]._default` → `_default` → the flat form. A bare `{ min, max }` is a range, not a type map. A named entry beats the QA `lists` profile while the catch-all loses to it; a `relations` entry beats both for a relationship field. `listSize` never grows a pool — raise `count` for that — and an unknown type, unknown field or non-list field throws a `TypeError`. Default `{ min: 1, max: 5 }`.
- `uniqueLists` option (`UniqueListsConfig`, default `true`): scalar and enum lists are drawn **without replacement**, the way relationship lists always were, so nothing a component keys by repeats. The length gives way to that: a `[Colour!]!` over a three-value enum yields at most three entries whatever `listSize` says, and a scalar generator that runs out of distinct values (a constant `scalars` entry, a QA text profile) returns a short list rather than spinning — each slot re-draws at most 12 times. Object-valued scalars (`JSON`) dedupe by their JSON form. `false`, or a map in the same shape as `listSize` (`{ Post: { tags: false }, _default: true }`, resolved `[type][field]` → `[type]._default` → `_default` → the flat form), asks for the repeats back; a named entry outranks the catch-all. Defaults to `false` under `qa` because the QA corpora are tiny and deduping would cap a `lists: 'huge'` profile at the size of the corpus. An unknown type, unknown field or non-list field throws a `TypeError`.
- `countFields` option (`boolean | { [type]: { [countField]: listField } }`): pairs a count scalar with the list it counts and sizes that list to the pool of what it holds, so `totalCount` is a total of something a pager can page through. Pairing is by name (`postCount`/`numberOfPosts`/`totalPosts` → `posts`; a nameless `total`/`count`/`totalCount` → the type's single object list, Relay `totalCount` → `edges`), and a map adds the pairings the convention misses. An explicit `relations` size, an `overrides` entry for the count, and a `derive` for the same field all still win. Under a QA `lists` profile the profile owns the sizing and this only syncs the counts; `countFields: false` turns it off. With `matchArguments`, a paired count on a wrapper type follows the narrowing — it reports the rows the filters left (before paging), so a filtered list doesn't sit under an unfiltered total; paging alone leaves it at the pool size. A count beside a plain list field, rather than on a wrapper, still reports what was wired.
- `defineScenarios(map)` / `composeScenarios(...scenarios)`: a scenario is a named partial `BuildMocksOptions` (plus `description`), passed as `scenario: Scenario | Scenario[]` and applied left to right with the explicit options last. Maps merge key by key (`count` per type, `overrides`/`derive`/`relations`/`countFields` two levels deep, `scalars` by name, `qa` per dimension); everything else is last-wins. `defineScenarios` is an identity function — `defineScenarios<SchemaTypeMap>()({ … })` binds it to a type map (or add `satisfies ScenarioMap<SchemaTypeMap>`), and `composeScenarios<SchemaTypeMap>(a, b)` checks every piece against that map and returns a `Scenario<SchemaTypeMap>`.
- `buildMatrix(schema, options?)`: crosses a `scenarios` map with `qaPresets` and returns a flat `MatrixCell[]` (`name`, `scenario`, `qa`, `options`, `mocks`). Either axis may be omitted. Each cell gets its own faker seeded from `seed` (`seedPerCell` opts out), and with `stableIds` each cell's ids are prefixed with a slug of its name unless `idPrefix` is set. `buildQaSets` is the QA-only shorthand over the same engine.
- `buildQaSets(schema, options?)`: QA mode. Returns one `{ name, qa, mocks }` set per profile (`QA_PROFILE_NAMES`, or a `profiles` subset), each built from its own seeded faker so a set reproduces independently of the others. Accepts every `BuildMocksOptions` key plus `profiles` and a shared `qa` config the profile merges over.
- `qa` option (`QaProfileName | QaConfig | false`): swaps generators for deliberately out-of-norm values across five dimensions — `text` (`empty`/`whitespace`/`long`/`unicode`/`injection`), `lists` (`empty`/`single`/`huge`, sized by `listSize`, default 100), `nulls` (`none`/`all`/`mixed`), `numbers` (`zero`/`negative`/`boundary`), `dates` (`epoch`/`farPast`/`farFuture`/`mixed`). `scalars` and `overrides` still win; `ID` is left alone; built-in scalars stay serializable but custom scalar constraints are not respected.
- `matchArguments` option (`boolean | ArgMatchingOptions`, default `false`): interprets three buckets only — equality against a same-named scalar/enum field (including inside nested input objects), search args, and paging. Wrapper and connection types are unwrapped so the arguments apply to the list inside them (`unwrap`, `listPath`), an unrecognized active argument becomes a deterministic partition key so aliased selections of the same field differ (`partition: false` to opt out), and an emptied list stays empty rather than being refilled from the pool.
- `argOverrides` option (`ArgOverride[]`): answer one field by its argument values — `{ match: { type?, field, args?, predicate? }, data }`, first match wins, `data` a value or a function of `{ typeName, fieldName, args, pool, isList, faker }`. `match.field` is the schema field name, never the alias. Every other field of the operation still resolves from the graph. Applies whether or not `matchArguments` is on.
- `@vantreeseba/graphql-mocks-codegen` plugin: emits `export type SchemaTypeMap = { … }` for every object type (root operation and introspection types excluded, entries sorted).

## Examples

- Basic: `const mocks = buildMocks(schema); mocks.User; mocks.Todo;` — 5 of each, with `todo.user` pointing into `mocks.User`.
- Deterministic + per-type counts: `buildMocks(schema, { seed: 42, count: { User: 10, Todo: 50, _default: 5 }, nullChance: 0.1 })`.
- Custom scalar mockers: `buildMocks(schema, { scalars: { DateTime: (f) => f.date.recent().toISOString(), CityName: (f) => f.location.city() } })`.
- Field overrides (receive the seeded faker and `{ index, typeName, fieldName }`): `buildMocks(schema, { overrides: { User: { name: () => 'Alice', loginCount: (f, { index }) => index === 0 ? 0 : f.number.int(500) } } })`.
- Derived fields (the finished object): `buildMocks(schema, { derive: { User: { fullName: (self) => `${self.firstName} ${self.lastName}` }, Cart: { total: (self) => self.items.length } } })`.
- Correlated fields from one draw: `buildMocks(schema, { deriveObject: { Order: (_self, { faker }) => { const subtotal = faker.number.float({ min: 10, max: 500 }); const tax = subtotal * 0.08; return { subtotal, tax, total: subtotal + tax }; } } })`.
- Stable ids: `buildMocks(schema, { stableIds: true }).User[0]` → `{ __typename: 'User', id: 'User-0', … }`; every other string field the library reads as an identifier (`id` in any casing, or a name ending in `Id`/`ID`) gets `TypeName-<field>-<index>`, e.g. `paymentMethodId: 'PaymentMethod-paymentMethodId-0'`. `stableIds: ['code']`, or `{ Currency: ['code'] }`, adds the names the convention misses.
- Interfaces/unions: `buildMocks(schema, { resolveType: (name) => name === 'SearchResult' ? 'Post' : 'User' })`.
- Typed pools: `buildMocks<{ User: User; Todo: Todo }>(schema)` or `buildMocks<SchemaTypeMap>(schema)`.
- Operation data: `const data = mocks.dataForOperation(UserByIdQuery)` → `{ user: { …selected fields, nested via wired refs… } }`.
- Apollo MockedProvider (data from the graph): `<MockedProvider mocks={[mocks.mockOperation(AwardByIdQuery)]} />`.
- A whole client for a test or story: `const client = createMockClient(mocks, { delay: 300, matchArguments: true })`, then render under `<ApolloProvider client={client}>`.
- Storybook: `withGraphqlMocks((options) => buildMocks(schema, { seed: 1, ...options }), { wrap: (client, Story) => <ApolloProvider client={client}><Story /></ApolloProvider> })`, with stories setting `parameters: { graphqlMocks: 'loading' | { qa: 'longText' } | false }`.
- A story set derived from one base parameter: `const base = { overrides: [orderFixture] }`, then `parameters: { graphqlMocks: withState(base, 'loading') }` / `withQa(base, 'longText')` — writing `'loading'` there instead drops the base's overrides silently.
- Validating hand-written mocks: `import * as mocks from './mocks'; it('are well formed', () => assertValidMocks(mocks))`.
- Serializing a pooled object: `JSON.stringify(toPlain(mocks.User[0]))`, or `select(mocks.User[0], UserRowFragmentDoc)` for a document-shaped view.
- QA mode, single profile: `buildMocks(schema, { seed: 42, qa: 'longText' })` or tuned: `buildMocks(schema, { qa: { text: 'unicode', lists: 'huge', nulls: 'mixed' } })`.
- QA sets for Storybook/Apollo: `buildQaSets(schema, { seed: 42 }).map((set) => ({ name: set.name, parameters: { apolloClient: { mocks: [set.mocks.mockOperation(UsersQuery)] } } }))`.
- `paginateArgs(items, ctx, options?)`: the search-and-page preamble an `argOverrides` handler otherwise writes by hand. Reads the offset, page size and search term out of `ctx.args` using the same names the argument matcher does (exported as `DEFAULT_OFFSET_ARGS` = skip/offset, `DEFAULT_LIMIT_ARGS` = limit/first/take, `DEFAULT_SEARCH_ARGS` = search/query/q/filter/searchTerm/term), and returns `{ items, matchedCount, totalCount, skip, limit, search }`. Options: `searchFields`, `offsetArgs`, `limitArgs`, `searchArgs`, `defaultLimit`, `flattenInputs` (one level, so `where: { search }` is found). No page size means unpaged, not empty.
- Relationship shaping: `buildMocks(schema, { relations: { User: { todos: 0, posts: { min: 1, max: 2 } }, Post: { comments: 'all', author: ({ pool }) => pool[0] }, Query: { users: 3 } } })`.
- Coherent wrapper totals: `buildMocks(schema, { count: { _default: 40 }, countFields: true })` — `results` holds all 40 pooled products and `totalCount` reports 40.
- Named scenarios: `const scenarios = defineScenarios({ newUser: { count: { User: 1 }, relations: { User: { todos: null } }, overrides: { User: { loginCount: () => 0 } } } }); buildMocks(schema, { scenario: scenarios.newUser, seed: 42 })`.
- Scenario × QA matrix: `buildMatrix(schema, { scenarios, qaPresets: [false, 'longText', 'hugeLists'], seed: 42 })` → one cell per combination, named `"newUser × longText"`.
- Argument matching (opt-in): `buildMocks(schema, { matchArguments: true })` — `user(id: "User-2")`, `users(skip: 10, limit: 5)` and `posts(titleContains: "x")` select data; unmatched lists return `[]`, unmatched singulars fall back to a random pick, and auto-filled variables are ignored.
- Answering one field by its argument: `buildMocks(schema, { argOverrides: [{ match: { field: 'items', args: { where: 'LOW_STOCK' } }, data: lowStockRows }] })`.
- Any-operation transport: `new ApolloClient({ cache, link: mockLink(mocks) })`, or `await mocks.toRequestHandler()({ query, variables })`.
- Story states: `const s = mockScenarios({}, 'UserById'); mocks.toRequestHandler(s.loading)`.
